title: QBR + Renewal Runbook: Dedicated → Private & SLA Expansion Plays
body:
Purpose and scope:

This runbook is a lightweight QBR + renewal playbook focused on systematic expansion motions: moving customers from hosted to Dedicated, enabling Private deployments for regulated workloads, and selling premium SLA add-ons. Target audience: CSMs handling mid-market and enterprise accounts, solutions engineers who support technical qualification, and AE/AM partners who will assist on contract & pricing.

Top-level goals (what success looks like):
- Convert eligible hosted customers to Dedicated or Private with low friction and clear TCO story.
- Add premium SLA for accounts with latency/uptime commitments >99.9% or enterprise purchasing needs.
- Reduce renewal churn by preemptively addressing scale, security, and cost questions.
- Create repeatable QBR agenda and follow-up artifacts that feed into renewal forecasts and PS opportunities.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Run the renewal tracker export before the QBR (fields listed below).
2) Prep a tailored QBR slide: usage + cost trends, reliability incidents, ops or infra asks, product roadmap alignment.
3) Run the qualification checklist with Solutions Eng during pre-call.
4) Execute play sequence (Tiered) and log outcomes to the tracker.

QBR agenda template (35–45 min):
- 5m Intro & objectives (CS owner + AE)
- 7m Health snapshot: API call trends, p50/p95 latency, error rate, token spend (this quarter vs prior)
- 7m Reliability & incidents: recent outages, mitigations, runbooks, escalation paths
- 6m Roadmap alignment: features impacting performance, data residency, rollout windows
- 6m Expansion opportunities: Dedicated capacity, Private deployment feasibility, SLA needs (pricing ranges)
- 4m Risk & renewal readiness: contract timelines, stakeholder map, procurement blockers
- 5m Next steps & owners (clear dates)

QBR prep checklist (CS owner):
- Pull usage/latency/cost dashboard and trend slides (Console -> Customer -> Metrics)
- Export prefix/KV cache hit rates and any throttling events
- Confirm model(s) in use and their verified performance profile
- Run the "Dedicated fit" checklist (below) with SE and tag recommended config
- Draft one-line ROI/efficiency statement for Dedicated/private migration (e.g., 30% reduction in per-token infra cost for stable workloads)

Renewal & expansion tracker columns (CSV-friendly):
account_id,account_name,renewal_date,current_contract_type,current_monthly_spend,avg_monthly_tokens,primary_contact,procurement_owner,legal_status,CSM,AE,health_score,p95_latency_ms,errors_last_90d,dedicated_candidate_score,private_candidate_score,potential_annual_value,next_qbr_date,expansion_stage,notes,last_touch_date

Sample expansion stages (canonical):
- 0 - Unqualified
- 1 - Qualified (SE validation needed)
- 2 - Business case created (CS + AE draft)
- 3 - Technical validation in progress (PoC or lab test)
- 4 - Commercial terms negotiated
- 5 - Contract signed / Migration scheduled

Qualification checklist (SE + CS):
- Workload stability: >30% of usage from repeat/steady traffic (yes/no)
- Latency sensitivity: requires p95 < X ms for core flows (yes/no, target value)
- Data residency/compliance: needs VPC or on-prem (yes/no)
- Throughput needs: sustained token/sec > threshold on hosted tier (number)
- Is there a preferred on-prem cloud partner or private region? (notes)
- Integration complexity: containerized models, custom kernels, or third-party infra (low/med/high)
- Security/KMS requirements: HSM/KMS needed (Y/N)
- Budget approvals: finance engaged (Y/N)

Dedicated upgrade play (short-form):
1) Score fit (use dedicated_candidate_score 0-100).
2) Create the TCO slide comparing current per-token hosted cost vs Dedicated commit with examples (30/60/90 day smoothing). Include burst vs steady assumptions.
3) Offer a 90-day trial/discounted reserved capacity pilot with known bands and exit criteria.
4) SE runs a synthetic load test using customer query distribution. Capture latency and throughput.
5) If pilot passes, AE/CS propose a reserved capacity term with onboarding checkpoints and migration runbook.

Private deployment play (short-form):
1) Business alignment: confirm data residency, compliance needs, or legal demands for private control plane.
2) Scope technical prerequisites: network topology, KMS, ingress/egress rules, audit log forwarding, offline provisioning windows.
3) Offer staged plan: Dev sandbox (2–4 weeks) -> Staging validation (2–6 weeks) -> Prod cutover (scheduled).
4) Identify Redwood internal stakeholders: private-deployments eng lead, solutions eng, security reviewer.
5) Create statement of work (SOW) and attach migration milestones + handover to SRE/ops.

Premium SLA add-on play (short-form):
- Target accounts that: a) have uptime contract needs >99.9%, b) face regulatory penalties on downtime, or c) are migrating mission-critical flows.
- Offer tiered SLA bundles (bronze/silver/gold) with response/restore windows and priced uplift.
- Attach runbook obligations: scheduled maintenance windows, notification lead times, test drills per year.
- Require health & observability checklist to be met prior to SLA activation.

Talk tracks & objection handling (snippets to use):
- "Why Dedicated?" -> "Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and cost — we model your committed capacity and show per-token economics vs on-demand spikes."
- "We're worried about migration risk." -> "We run a pilot with no long-term commitment, provide detailed runbooks, and our SEs will shadow the migration end-to-end."
- "SLA uplift seems expensive." -> "Think of SLA as insurance: for mission-critical features that carry regulatory risk, the cost of a single outage often dwarfs annual SLA fees. We can tier features into SLA scope to reduce cost."

Technical artifacts to prepare (attach to QBR follow-up):
- Current usage export (CSV) + representative query sample (anonymized)
- Synthetic load test results and interpretation notes
- Proposed dedicated capacity profile (GPUs, instance types, autoscale policy)
- Private deployment checklist (network & security tasks)
- Draft SOW and example pricing bands

Internal handoffs & roles:
- CSM: owner of QBR and customer success narrative; primary point for business case and follow-ups
- AE/AM: commercial negotiation and contract drafting
- Solutions Eng: technical qualification, load testing, PoC
- Private Deployments Eng: deployment plan and infra sign-off
- Legal/Procurement: contract and compliance checks

Risk flags (early signs of churn or blockers):
- Sudden drop in usage without product changes
- Multiple unresolved reliability incidents in last 90 days
- Finance or procurement delays beyond 2 sprints of the renewal date
- High error rates on primary endpoints or model regressions reported by product QA

Sample follow-up email (short):
Subject: QBR follow-up & next steps -- [Account]
Hi [Name],
Thanks for the time today — attached are the slide deck and the pilot proposal we discussed for Dedicated capacity. Per our call, next steps: 1) SE team will schedule load test (by 2026-03-02), 2) AE to share pilot pricing (by 2026-03-05), 3) CS will send updated migration runbook (by 2026-03-09).
I'll keep ownership of the timeline; let me know if procurement should be looped in earlier.
Best,
Aisha

Playbook KPIs to track (CS dashboard):
- # of pilots started per quarter (goal: 6 for mid-market)
- Conversion rate from pilot -> paid Reserved (goal: 45%)
- Time from first qualification -> contract signed (goal: 60 days median)
- SLA attach rate at renewal (goal: 25% for eligible accounts)
- Churn rate for accounts with active expansion discussions vs baseline

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Need a short decision-tree visual for quick qualification (low effort to produce, high signal).
- Can we standardize a 90-day reserved pilot contract template with legal? Current turnaround varies by region.
- Explore bundling health monitoring + SLA to increase attach rate without large price jump.

Appendix: quick scripts / queries to pull data (copy-paste for SE/CS):
- API usage by prefix last 90 days: SELECT prefix, SUM(tokens) FROM usage WHERE customer_id = ? GROUP BY prefix ORDER BY SUM(tokens) DESC
- Latency percentiles: use p95 from trace logs grouped by model and route

End of draft runbook. This should serve as a working artifact for CS + SE to iterate on before we finalize the standardized QBR slide pack and pilot contract templates.
